extracted.intended_audience: foreign lecturers, teachers, missionaries and public speakers addressing Japanese audiences
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and evaluative criteria for delivering lectures and conducting teaching or public addresses in Japan, focusing on audience expectations, etiquette, interpretation logistics, and desired speaker qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker qualities prized by Japanese audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: With such minds, clearness, knowledge of his subject, and moral earnestness on the part of the speaker, are the most highly prized qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that clearness, subject mastery, and moral earnestness win regard; appreciation and enthusiasm follow upon conviction of the truthfulness of what is said. The true-hearted teacher values this recognition more highly than temporary applause or popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect secretiveness and restrained emotional display
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain 'secretiveness,' or demeanour due to trained habit of repressing the emotions, at least until they break forth into more emphatic or even extravagant form because of long-continued repression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repression (linked to samurai training) means visible emotional responses may be muted; speakers should not infer lack of feeling or engagement from an absence of visible emotion. Examples compare Japanese quietness favorably against more demonstrative audiences (e.g., Russians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Native listening manner: patient, polite, respectful, and silent
rubrics_metrics.description: The truly native manner of listening is an unflinchingly patient, polite, and respectful, but silent attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect frequent audible signs of approval (clapping etc. is more common in Westernized institutions like YMCA). Silence is often a mark of respect rather than indifference; speakers can be deceived about audience reaction if they expect Western-style feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary patience and endurance in audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Another marked characteristic of Japanese audiences is their extraordinary patience in listening... the listeners seem to feel the obligation to maintain the same attitude of attention to the very end of the discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audiences often remain for very long sessions (examples: nearly 1,000 officials for >2 hours; 1,500 citizens for ~3 hours). Speakers should be prepared for long formats and should not expect audiences to leave early as in some other cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation logistics: divide lecture for alternating translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The customary method was to divide the entire address into five or six parts of about ten minutes each; and then lecturer and interpreter alternated in regular order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for roughly double the time when English is interpreted into Japanese; plan short, modular segments to facilitate smooth interpretation. Alternatively, a highly skilled interpreter may render the whole lecture afterward in fluent Japanese, but this is the exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware speakers can be deceived about audience judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The disadvantage... is this: he may be utterly unaware, or completely deceived, as to the way in which his audience is taking him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of silent attention and restraint, solicit other cues or arrange for feedback/interpretation summaries to gauge reception; do not rely on applause or visible enthusiasm as the only indicators of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect critical independence, especially among students
rubrics_metrics.description: The tendency to revolt from authority and to appeal to the rational judgment of the individual has been the inevitable accompaniment of the transition from the Old to the New Japan... this tendency has been greatest and most conspicuous among the student classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers should be prepared for coolness of demeanour and independent critique from student audiences; authoritative rhetoric alone may not win approval—reasoned argument and appeal to judgment are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid teaching for popularity; prioritize educative value
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambition... to have large classes and to get into the class-books of the Seniors as a 'favourite' or 'most popular' teacher, is one of the several baleful results of the excessive lengths to which the elective system has been carried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns against instructors seeking popularity at the expense of substantive education; speakers and teachers should focus on clear, earnest instruction rather than popularity-seeking tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to pupils' mental and moral culture, not only reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: With them the tendency of the professors and other instructors is to become too exclusively interested in their own reputation for science... and to care too little for the mental and moral culture of the great body of their pupils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors are advised to balance scholarly reputation with responsibility for students' broader moral and intellectual development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build long-term relationships through competence, devotion, and tact
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreigner, therefore, who enters into scholastic relations with Japanese students, if he is competent, devoted and tactful, need not concern himself greatly about this part of the returns from his labours; it will surely follow in due time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful teachers receive deep, lasting gratitude (compared to filial bonds); sustained competence and tact yield strong personal and professional rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and accept local etiquette and ceremonial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The demands of etiquette, which are somewhat more inexorable in Japan than with us... To have declined to receive it would have resulted in a grievous disappointment to many others, and might even have occasioned a breach of friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offered escorts, ceremonies, or public honours, refusing can offend—accepting local forms of courtesy (even when inconvenient) preserves relationships. Example: large, ceremonious 'Sayonara' processions and escorts despite poor weather; do not decline without care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for bilingual delivery time costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Of this more than two hours of speaking and listening, somewhat less than one-half was usually occupied by the lecture in English; while the Japanese paraphrase, in order to make all clear, required the remainder of the allotted time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When lectures are rendered into Japanese, expect the session length to expand significantly; schedule accordingly and coordinate with interpreters about pacing and segmentation.
